claim: For every integer \(n\ge 1\), let \(K_{2,n}\) be the complete bipartite graph with left vertices \(u,v\) and right vertices \(w_0,\ldots,w_{n-1}\). Its ordinary Morse complex \(\mathcal M(K_{2,n})\), whose simplices are acyclic discrete vector fields, satisfies \(\mathcal M(K_{2,n})\simeq\bigvee^{n^2-1}S^n\), with the empty wedge at \(n=1\) interpreted as a point. An explicit sequential element matching has one critical \(0\)-simplex and exactly \(n^2-1\) critical \(n\)-simplices, and no other critical cells.
integrity: The unbounded statement is proved by an explicit sequential element matching and an induction describing all surviving faces. The included verifier exhaustively checks the face model, critical-cell formulas, Euler characteristic, and finite acyclicity tests through the stated ranges; finite computation is corroboration, not the infinite proof.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is restricted to the ordinary Morse complex of \(K_{2,n}\). It does not determine the complete-bipartite family with both parts at least three, nor generalized or pure Morse complexes. A residual bibliographic risk is an equivalent older formulation in directed-tree language not surfaced by the checked exact-family literature.
title: The Morse complex of \(K_{2,n}\) is a wedge of \(n^2-1\) \(n\)-spheres
